The last monarch from Britain’s House of Hanover was **King William IV**.  
He died on **20 June 1837** at Windsor Castle.  After his death, the Hanoverian line continued in the Kingdom of Hanover (his brother Ernest Augustus became king), but the personal union with Britain ended, and Queen Victoria succeeded him on the British throne.  (Source: *Wikipedia – William IV of the United Kingdom*.)

**William IV** (William Henry; 21 August 1765– 20 June 1837) was [King of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland] and [King of Hanover] from 26 June 1830 until his death in 1837. The third son of [George III], William succeeded his elder brother [George IV], becoming the last king and penultimate monarch of the United Kingdom's [House of Hanover].

William served in the [Royal Navy] in his youth, spending time in [British North America] and the [Caribbean], and was later nicknamed the "Sailor King". In 1789, he was created [Duke of Clarence and St Andrews]. Between 1791 and 1811, he cohabited with the actress [Dorothea Jordan], with whom he had ten children. In 1818, he married [Princess Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen]. He was appointed Britain's [Lord High Admiral] in 1827, the first since 1709.

As his two elder brothers died without leaving [legitimate] "Legitimacy (family law)") issue, William [inherited the throne] when he was 64 years old. His reign saw several reforms: the [Poor Law] was updated, [child labour] restricted, [slavery abolished] in nearly all of the [British Empire], and the electoral system refashioned by the [Reform Act 1832]. Although William did not engage in politics as much as his brother or his father, he was the last British monarch to appoint a prime minister contrary to the will of [Parliament]. He granted [his German kingdom] a short-lived liberal constitution. William had no surviving legitimate children at the time of his death, so he was succeeded by his niece [Victoria] in the United Kingdom and his brother [Ernest Augustus] in Hanover, ending the 123-year [personal union] between the two countries.
